shorts.title: What you will learn: Pointers and arrays
shorts.hook: An array name quietly turns into a pointer.
shorts.script: An array name quietly turns into a pointer. Today we connect arrays and pointers. They look different, but they work together all the time. In most places, an array name turns into the address of its first item. We call this array decay. So you can store the array name in a pointer. Then p index i works like a index i. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Pointers and arrays in one minute
shorts.hook: In most places, an array name turns into the address of its first item.
shorts.script: In most places, an array name turns into the address of its first item. We call this array decay. So you can store the array name in a pointer. Then p index i works like a index i. But there is a cost. A pointer does not know the size of the array. Think of the first house on a street. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: Q starts at the first item.
shorts.script: Q starts at the first item. A plus three is the address right after the last item. The loop stops when q reaches it. Q plus plus moves q to the next item. Each round prints the item that q points to. The program prints ten, twenty and thirty on one line. An array name turns into the address of its first item. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Sizeof on an array parameter
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The function tries to count the items with sizeof. The compiler warns that sizeof on an array parameter returns the size of a pointer. The array decayed to a pointer, and the size was lost. Pass the size as a second parameter. An array parameter is a pointer in disguise. Sizeof then gives the size of the pointer, not the size of the array. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Sizeof on an array parameter.
